reason: Role is readable from the code but the axis fails the fit test, so no name. Post-injection path of cm848_calculateEngineFaultTiming: x = fuel_quantity_axis2_index (interval from the main event to the third event: angle difference x crank period / (cam_sync_position_high_byte * 256), then >> 3 = 3.2 us counts), y = fuel_quantity_table_result (main on-time in 0.4 us ticks); the result times the L023 value >> 4 is added to the post quantity engine_timing_delta, only while the main on-time is nonzero. That makes it the post-injection twin of L065 (pilot path). But the x axis 0x5f8ac holds 0..9 with repeats (0,0,1,1,1,2,2,2,3,3,4,4,4,5,5,5,6,6,6,7,7,8,8,8,9), and a third pulse is only enabled for an interval of at least fuel_injection_quantity_threshold = 1500 ticks (x >= 187), so every real input saturates the last breakpoint. The grid is all zero (inert in this calibration) and is read unsigned (flags 0) where L065 is read signed (flags 4), so the pairing with L065 cannot be confirmed from data. Candidate if the caller wants a name anyway: post_quantity_main_correction.

x = engine_timing_delta (post-injection fuel quantity) and y = fuel_pressure_sensor (axis 0..3276 = 0..1600 bar fits); the result is the first factor of the post quantity correction ((L023 x L022) >> 4 is added to the post quantity), parallel to L066 in the main path (same flags 6). Skipped because the grid is all zero, so the factor's role (a scale as in L066 or something else) cannot be confirmed from data, and the x axis runs to 4416 (375 mm3 at 11.776 counts/mm3) while the post on-time table L024 stops at 662 (56 mm3), so the axis does not look calibrated for this input. Candidate if promoted: post_quantity_main_correction_scale.

Forced to 0 unless the event starts at least fuel_injection_quantity_threshold (1500 ticks) after the main.
units_check: x axis (11 pts 0..662) = 0..56 mm3 at 11.776 counts/mm3; y axis (9 pts 184, 307, 410, 512, 615, 820, 1025, 2049, 3279) = 90, 150, 200, 250, 300, 400, 500, 1000, 1600 bar at 0.488 bar/count (round values); grid 0..7343 ticks. evidence: Third event of the cycle and after the main by computation: cm848_calculateEngineFaultTiming only enables it when angle(third) - angle(main) > 0 and, in timing mode 1 (the RAM dump value), that interval in ticks is at least 1500; its quantity engine_timing_delta is taken off the main quantity in cm848_calculateEngineTimingInterpolation and added back (main on-time recomputed) when this pulse comes out 0.
naming_concern: Legacy destination names are inverted for this family: injection_timing_active_flag is the post on-time in ticks (not a flag) and engine_timing_delta is its quantity, while the fuel_quantity_* names (fuel_quantity_active, fuel_quantity_table_result, fuel_quantity_trim) hold on-times too. cm848_calculateEngineFaultTiming and the injection_fault_timing_*_interp_state cache words describe the post injection, not a fault. cruise_speed_rate_of_change is the on-time cap (crank period / 16), not a cruise value.

naming_concern: Legacy destination names are inverted: fuel_quantity_table_result / fuel_quantity_active (and fuel_quantity_trim, injection_timing_active_flag) hold on-times in ticks, while engine_timing_reference* / engine_timing_delta / cam_timing_reference_offset hold fuel quantities. cm848_calculateTimingWithTables computes the main on-time, not a timing.
